passage: In the clinic waiting room, Rafiq's phone lit up with an email: reply to the offer by five today. Dilnaz saw the screen. Neither spoke. "That cricket match last night," Rafiq said. "Terrible." "Yes," said Dilnaz. All week they had done this, talking about the cricket, the cousin's wedding, the weather in other cities, anything but Lucknow. At four, in the car park, Rafiq said, "So we're taking it?" "I suppose. If you want." "If you want." It was settled in two minutes. Rafiq typed the reply while Dilnaz looked out of the window. Neither said what they were afraid of. On the drive home the silence was heavier than any argument would have been.

qa.q: What could the couple have done earlier in the week?
qa.a: They could have set aside time days before the deadline to say their fears out loud, so the choice was not squeezed into two minutes.

qa.q: How might the quick reply have felt to Dilnaz at the window?
qa.a: Dilnaz may have felt unheard and left with unspoken doubts, still holding worries that never got said.

grounding: Rafiq and Dilnaz keep changing the subject until the deadline arrives, and decide in a hurry with no talk of feelings.

passage:
Dear Vinita,

You asked how we decided about Doha. The honest answer is, we didn't really decide. It just happened.
When the offer came in March, Mariam and I both knew it was a big question. Her mother isn't well, and my career has been stuck here. But every time one of us started, the other found something else to talk about. Dinner, her cousin's wedding, anything. We told ourselves we were keeping the peace.
Then the company emailed: reply by Friday. On Thursday night, in forty tired minutes, we said yes. Mariam cried a little and said, "It's fine."
Now we're here, and I don't think it is fine. We never talked about what she's afraid of, or what she'd miss. We just saved ourselves from one hard conversation and bought ourselves a lot of quiet ones.
Tell me honestly if you think I should call her mother more.

Jomon

qa.q: When did Jomon and Mariam have to reply to the company?
How did Mariam seem to feel on the Thursday night?
qa.a: Mariam seemed sad and uneasy; she cried a little and said "It's fine" in a way that didn't sound fine.

qa.q: What else could Jomon and Mariam have done when the offer first came in March?
qa.a: They could have set a calm time to talk about fears and hopes, weeks before the deadline, instead of changing the subject.

qa.q: How is Mariam affected by the hurried decision?
qa.a: Mariam moved without her fears or losses being heard, so she may feel unheard and lonely in Doha, far from her unwell mother.

grounding: It shows a couple avoiding a difficult topic to keep peace until the offer deadline forces a hurried decision with little talk about feelings.

subtopic: A marriage disagreement over careers or location

passage:
Bidisha, you want to know why I look so unsettled lately? I'll tell you. I'm Ishita, and we moved to Bengaluru without ever really talking about it.
Rohit got the offer in January. We both knew it would mean leaving Kolkata, my parents, my NGO work. But neither of us wanted a fight. He'd bring it up and I'd say, "Let's see." I'd bring it up and he'd switch on the cricket.
Then the HR email said: confirm by Monday. On Sunday night, over dal and rice, we said yes in about half an hour. I nodded a lot. I don't think I said one thing I actually felt.
Now we're here. Rohit loves his team. And I sit in this flat wondering why I never told him how scared I was of losing my work.
We kept the peace, Bidisha. And now it's too quiet.

qa.q: When did the HR email ask them to confirm by?
How does Ishita feel now in Bengaluru?
qa.a: Ishita feels unsettled and lonely, regretting never sharing the fear of losing the NGO work.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Ishita and Rohit handled the offer?
qa.a: Set a calm time to talk properly about fears and hopes soon after the offer, instead of avoiding it until the deadline.

qa.q: How might Rohit see the move now?
qa.a: Rohit loves his new team and may not realise how scared Ishita was, since those feelings were never discussed.

grounding: It shows a couple avoiding a disagreement to keep peace until the offer deadline forces a hurried decision with little discussion of feelings.
